Windows local system features usage detected
 Mandatory 3

Explanation

Windows local system features usage detected.

Managed Instance on App Service allows use of registry adapters (Key Vault-backed) for config; replace local process launching with Functions/Jobs; route file I/O to storage mounts. Use Bastion RDP only for diagnostics and persist changes via scripts.

Windows features like registry access, starting processes via shell, access to COM objects, using standard OS dialogs etc, will be restricted on Azure App Service. This indicates that your application might be broken in App Service sandbox environment or not scale well.

If you choose to use containerized Azure hosting options with Windows container, such as Azure AppService sandbox for Windows container, Azure Container Apps (ACA) or Azure Kubernetes Service (AKS), some scenarios might work, however scaling still might be an issue.

Recommendations:
1. Avoid using Windows registry or default Windows UI elements and dialogs.
2. If your application needs to read app-specific configuration, you can use the App Settings feature of Azure App Service, which allows you to store key-value pairs of configuration data for your application. You can access these settings from your code using environment variables. Another option is to use Azure App Configuration and Azure Key Vault to share application settings in a cloud-native way.
3. If your application is writing data (like machine-wide settings cache), use an external data store like Azure SQL DB or Azure Cache for Redis.
4. Instead of starting local worker processes use Azure Functions.

IO operations outside of the application folder might not be available on Azure App Service. Possible solutions:

2. Other services that the application depends on might need to be migrated to Azure, this way you will get the benefit of lower latency in the cloud.
3. If your application needs to depend on services that run on-premise, you can connect your Azure and local networks with ExpressRoute, Hybrid Connections, or VPN solutions.

Architecture Diagram

Reporting.Legacy.Web is a single ASP.NET Web Forms application with an ASMX export endpoint. Its reporting logic accesses SQL Server directly and falls back to demo data when the live source fails.

Data Storage & External Services

The configured ODBC connection points to SQL Server Express and queries dbo.Orders. CSV exports are written to the configured local export root; the UNC archive root is displayed or returned as metadata, not written to by the application. Windows Registry and Event Log provide workstation metadata and best-effort logging. Session state is in-process; no external cache, message broker, or outbound API is declared in the inspected application.

Key Architectural Decisions

  • Web Forms code-behind and the ASMX service contain SQL and reporting logic directly rather than using a separate repository or service layer.
  • Both reporting paths fall back to demo data on ODBC errors; the report page also falls back when no rows are returned.
  • Windows authentication is configured, but authorization explicitly allows all users for the local demo; sessions are stored in process.

DTOs & Contracts

ExportResult is a mutable service-level response class; the operation takes two primitive integer parameters, not a request DTO. MonthlySales.MonthlySalesRow is a mutable presentation model bound to the report grid, not a gateway aggregation DTO. No gateway-level DTOs, OpenAPI/Swagger, protobuf, GraphQL schemas, or custom serializer configuration were found; ASMX supplies the service serialization. See data-architecture.md for data model details if available. Sources: Services/ReportExport.asmx.cs, Reports/MonthlySales.aspx.cs, Reporting.Legacy.Web.csproj, Web.config.

Communication Patterns

  • The pages synchronously access SQL Server via ODBC; the export button directly constructs ReportExport and calls it in-process. Remote ASMX calls are synchronous request/response. There is no identified message broker, asynchronous messaging, gateway, service discovery, client load balancing, or cross-service aggregation.
  • Report reads fall back to demo rows on query errors or an empty result. Export query errors produce demo CSV rows and a diagnostic row instead of failing the export; file, registry and other failures outside the query catch can propagate. Event Log write failures are swallowed. There are no explicit retries, circuit breakers, timeouts, bulkheads, or downstream-service fallback policies in source.
  • Windows authentication mode is configured, but authorization explicitly allows all users; there are no application role checks. Actual authentication also depends on host configuration. No HTTPS binding or TLS requirement is configured in the repository; the README's local example uses HTTP, and host-level TLS cannot be inferred. No service startup ordering is specified.

Core Business Workflows

The application lets back-office operators view a customer-level sales summary and export order data to CSV. It can substitute demonstration data when the live reporting source is unavailable.

The solution contains one project. There is no separate customer or order service, or cross-context exchange established by the repository. Sources: Reporting.Legacy.Web.sln, Reports/MonthlySales.aspx.cs, Services/ReportExport.asmx.cs.

Primary Workflows

Workflow 1: View sales summary

  1. The operator opens /Reports/MonthlySales.aspx; on the initial request the page records the last reporting page in session and queries the orders source.
  2. The query groups all orders by customer identifier and calculates order count and total sales. Despite the page title, it contains no month or year filter.
  3. If reading fails, the page displays an error message and appends demo rows; an empty result also causes demo rows to be shown. If a failure happens after some rows were read, those rows remain alongside the demo rows.
  4. The resulting rows are bound to the grid. A postback does not rerun this initial-load query.

Sources: Reports/MonthlySales.aspx, Reports/MonthlySales.aspx.cs.

Workflow 2: Export orders

  1. The operator clicks the export button on /Reports/MonthlySales.aspx; the page directly calls ExportOrders with the current UTC year and month. An external ASMX caller may supply those integers instead.
  2. The service reads configuration and the workstation registry value, creates the output directory, and reads all orders from the ODBC source. The supplied year and month select the filename, not the queried records.
  3. On an ODBC query exception, it appends demo records and an exception-type diagnostic row to any CSV data already accumulated. An empty successful query produces a header-only CSV.
  4. The service writes the CSV, attempts an informational Event Log entry, and returns ExportResult. The page displays the status and output path. The archive root is returned as metadata; no archive copy is performed.

Sources: Reports/MonthlySales.aspx.cs, Services/ReportExport.asmx.cs.

Cross-Service Data Flows

There are no independently deployed application services or gateway composition flows in the solution. Both workflows read the same external orders source directly through ODBC; the export additionally writes a local filesystem path. The demo-data branches described above are local source-read fallbacks, not circuit-breaker or inter-service fallbacks. Sources: Reporting.Legacy.Web.sln, Reports/MonthlySales.aspx.cs, Services/ReportExport.asmx.cs.

Business Rules & Decision Logic

  • Validation: ExportOrders accepts integer year and month values without explicit range or date validation. The page supplies current UTC values. No additional application-level business validators were found.
  • Calculations and selection: summary counts and sums are grouped by customer across all stored orders; export selects all orders. Neither query filters by the requested month or year. The export filename uses those values, formatting the month with at least two digits.
  • Fallback and errors: the summary uses demo data for errors or empty results, while export uses demo data only on exceptions. Both can retain partially read live rows before appending fallback data. Export filesystem or registry failures outside the query catch are not handled by the workflow.
  • State and integrity: the application records the last page in session, but no order lifecycle transitions, writes to orders, uniqueness rules, or explicit transaction boundaries are implemented. The CSV write can overwrite the same year/month filename.
  • Audit and authorization: startup and successful export attempt Event Log entries, with logging failures ignored. Windows authentication mode is configured, but authorization permits all users and no business role or resource-ownership checks are implemented.

Sources: Default.aspx.cs, Reports/MonthlySales.aspx.cs, Services/ReportExport.asmx.cs, Global.asax.cs, Web.config.

Version & Compatibility Risks

The project targets .NET Framework 4.7.2 and relies on System.Web and ASMX, which are not part of modern .NET's ASP.NET Core platform and require application changes for a move to modern .NET. Project references do not specify individual assembly versions; the framework target above is not a claim about their assembly version numbers. The project imports classic Visual Studio web application targets when available, which also affects build portability.
